## 02/10/2026 — First real prototype of the timer on a breadboard!

Today, I was finally able to make some real progress on the project. First, I understood that I needed to use both shift registers (SN74HC595) to make the display work correctly and more easily.

The wiring took a long time, and I had to do many checks... (one small resistor was not properly connected on the breadboard, which made me lose about an hour and a half!)

AI helped me a lot with the code. However, I still had to understand the whole logic behind the display, because the AI was not able to represent the numbers correctly on the display.

In the end, I managed to make a small test timer that starts automatically when the ESP32 is powered on and counts the seconds!

The next step will be to add a button so I can start and stop the timer. I also need to implement the feature that makes the display blink after every hour.
